sentences: In the 2006 film version of The Devil Wears Prada, Miranda Priestly, played by Meryl Streep, scolds her unattractive assistant for imagining that high fashion doesn’t affect her.

Priestly explains how the deep blue color of the assistant’s sweater descended over the years from fashion shows to department stores and to the bargain bin in which the poor girl doubtless found her garment.
translations: 在2006年的电影版《穿普拉达的女王》中，由梅丽尔·斯特里普饰演的米兰达·普里斯特利责备她那位不漂亮的助理，因为助理认为高级时尚对她没有影响。
普里斯特利解释了助理毛衣的深蓝色是如何多年来从时装秀一路降级到百货商店，再到那个可怜女孩无疑淘到这件衣服的廉价处理区的。

sentences: This top-down conception of the fashion business couldn’t be more out of date or at odds with the feverish world described in Overdressed, Elizabeth Cline’s three-year indictment of “fast fashion.”
In the last decade or so, advances in technology have allowed mass-market labels such as Zara, H&M, and Uniglo to react to trends more quickly and anticipate demand more precisely.
Quicker turnarounds mean less wasted inventory, more frequent releases, and more profit.
These labels encourage style-conscious consumers to see clothes as disposable—meant to last only a wash or two, although they don’t advertise that—and to renew their wardrobe every few weeks.
By offering on-trend items at dirt-cheap prices, Cline argues, these brands have hijacked fashion cycles, shaking an industry long accustomed to a seasonal pace.
translations: 这种自上而下的时尚产业观念已经过时得不能再过时了，也与伊丽莎白·克莱因在《过度着装》一书中所描述的狂热世界格格不入，该书是克莱因对“快时尚”为期三年的控诉。
在过去十年左右的时间里，技术的进步使得诸如Zara、H&M和优衣库等大众市场品牌能够更快地对潮流做出反应，并更精确地预测需求。
更快的周转意味着更少的库存浪费、更频繁的上新和更多的利润。
这些品牌鼓励注重时尚的消费者将衣服视为一次性用品——只打算洗一两次，尽管他们并不这样宣传——并且每隔几周就更新一次衣橱。
克莱因认为，通过以极低的价格提供时髦商品，这些品牌已经劫持了时尚周期，撼动了一个长期习惯于季节性节奏的行业。

sentences: The victims of this revolution, of course, are not limited to designers.

For H&M to offer a $5.95 knit miniskirt in all its 2,300-plus stores around the world, it must rely on low-wage overseas labor, order in volumes that strain natural resources, and use massive amounts of harmful chemicals.
translations: 当然，这场革命的受害者不仅限于设计师。
为了让H&M在全球2300多家门店提供一条5.95美元的针织迷你裙，它必须依赖海外廉价劳动力，以消耗自然资源的数量下单，并使用大量有害化学物质。

sentences: Overdressed is the fashion world’s answer to consumer-activist bestsellers like Michael Pollan’s The Omnivore’s Dilemma.
“Mass-produced clothing, like fast food, fills a hunger and need, yet is non-durable and wasteful,” Cline argues.
Americans, she finds, buy roughly 20 billion garments a year—about 64 items per person—and no matter how much they give away, this excess leads to waste.
translations: 《过度着装》是时尚界对迈克尔·波伦的《杂食者的困境》等消费者维权畅销书的回应。
克莱因认为：“大规模生产的服装，就像快餐一样，满足了饥饿和需求，但不耐用且浪费。”
她发现，美国人每年大约购买200亿件服装——每人约64件——无论他们捐赠多少，这种过度消费都会导致浪费。

sentences: Towards the end of Overdressed, Cline introduced her ideal, a Brooklyn woman named Sarah Kate Beaumont, who since 2008 has made all of her own clothes—and beautifully.
But as Cline is the first to note, it took Beaumont decades to perfect her craft; her example can’t be knocked off.
translations: 在《过度着装》的结尾，克莱因介绍了她的理想典范，一位名叫莎拉·凯特·博蒙特的布鲁克林女性，她自2008年以来一直自己制作所有衣服——而且做得很漂亮。
但正如克莱因首先指出的那样，博蒙特花了几十年时间才完善她的手艺；她的榜样无法被轻易模仿。

sentences: Though several fast-fashion companies have made efforts to curb their impact on labor and the environment—including H&M, with its green Conscious Collection line—Cline believes lasting change can only be effected by the customer.
She exhibits the idealism common to many advocates of sustainability, be it in food or in energy.
Vanity is a constant; people will only start shopping more sustainably when they can’t afford not to.
translations: 尽管几家快时尚公司已经努力减少其对劳动力和环境的影响——包括H&M及其“绿色自觉系列”——但克莱因认为，持久的改变只能由消费者来实现。
她展现了可持续性倡导者中常见的理想主义，无论是在食品还是能源领域。
虚荣心是永恒的；只有当人们无法承受不这样做时，他们才会开始更可持续地购物。
